intro: Adult social care helps people live with dignity, safety and independence, with the person always at the centre of everything you do.
points: Your duty of care is the legal and moral responsibility to keep people safe and act in their best interests.
Never carry out a task you have not been trained for, such as moving and handling; stop and ask when unsure.
If you believe someone is at risk of harm or abuse, you must pass the concern on; confidentiality is not absolute.
Give person-centred care: put the individual first, respect their choices, dignity and right to be involved in decisions.
Live the 6 Cs, the values that describe what good care looks like in your everyday practice.
Follow agreed ways of working — policies, care plans and risk assessments — and always use the most up-to-date version.
